title: Corpus Considerations for Annotator Modeling and Scaling

bias_targets.methodology: Comparing the performance of various annotator modeling and personalization techniques (e.g., user tokens, composite embeddings, multi-task learning) in predicting individual annotator labels versus aggregated majority-vote labels across seven subjective NLP datasets (e.g., hate speech, emotion recognition, social norms).

Evaluating the discrepancy between models trained to predict a single ground-truth majority label versus those capturing individual annotator perspectives, demonstrating how majority-vote aggregation marginalizes diverse or minority viewpoints in subjective tasks.
